Doctorate
The doctorate is a university examination that attains the highest academic degree, the doctoral degree. It is considered evidence of the ability to conduct independent scientific work and is required to continue to a Habilitation.
The doctorate is earned through an examination process governed by the Faculty’s doctoral regulations, in which the candidate must demonstrate their independent contribution to scientific research and development. These qualities are demonstrated with the acceptance of a written thesis (dissertation) and by passing an oral examination (scientific defense).
Doctorates are a mainstay of the research activities at Faculty III. They make an important contribution to the transfer and application of the latest scientific findings into practice and initiate innovative technical and social developments. Depending on the focus of the doctorate, the Faculty awards the Doctor of Engineering Sciences (Dr.-Ing.) or Doctor of Natural Sciences (Dr. rer. Nat.).
Current notices
Please note that revised doctoral regulations have been in effect since August 2023 and that new forms are therefore available. Please only use the forms available on the website. Please send all documents in advance by email.
Pursuing a doctorate at Faculty III
Expand all
Collapse all
Doctorate types and requirements
The formal requirement to become a doctoral candidate is the successful completion of a master’s degree program at a university, university of applied sciences (FH), or a comparable higher university degree (Diplom, Magister, Staatsexamen). Diplom graduates of universities of applied sciences may also be admitted to a doctorate if their final grade was above average (at least “good”) and they pass assessment tests. Holders of a bachelor’s degree with a particular aptitude for science can be admitted directly to a doctorate through an aptitude assessment procedure (direct track).
The doctoral degree demands the successful completion of a research paper (dissertation) and passing an oral examination (scientific defense). Depending on the focus of the doctorate, the Faculty awards the Doctor of Engineering Sciences (Dr.-Ing.) or Doctor of Natural Sciences (Dr. rer. Nat.).
Declaration of intent to pursue a doctorate
Doctoral candidates can and should declare their intent to pursue a doctorate as soon as they have a fully formulated research project (exposé) and a supervisor (Section 4 of the Doctoral Regulations (PromO)). It is particularly advisable for graduates of universities of applied sciences and graduates who studied outside Germany to register their intent so any matters regarding recognition of their qualifications can be clarified.
Aspiring doctoral candidates are to submit their application to the dean of Faculty III, specifying the working title of their dissertation and the subject area of the doctorate. Please use the Declaration of intent to pursue a doctorate to do so and include the following documents as attachments:
Tabular CV
Certified copy of your Diplom, bachelor’s or master’s certificate, and official diploma
Description of the proposed dissertation topic (exposé)
Work plan and time schedule
Copy of the supervision agreement
For Diplom graduates from universities of applies sciences: Diplom thesis and any other scientific work, if requested
Statistical data sheet
Your application will then be reviewed to confirm you meet the admission requirements. For applicants who studied outside Germany, the Department of International Affairs decides whether recognition is granted. If the applicant holds a Diplom from a university of applied science or their highest level of education is a bachelor’s degree, the examination and the determination of the examinations to be taken are carried out by the chairman of the examination board.
If you are not or no longer employed at TU Berlin, you must enroll as a doctoral candidate. The letter confirming acceptance of the declaration of intent to pursue a doctorate must be submitted to the Office of Student Affairs to enroll as a doctoral candidate. More information on enrollment can be found here.

Doctorate procedure
Opening of the doctoral procedure
Once you have completed your doctoral thesis, you can apply to the dean of Faculty III (via the Faculty Service Center) for admission to the doctoral procedure (Sections 5 and 6 PromO). Please use the application for admission to the doctoral procedure to do so. and include the following documents as attachments:
Four or five copies of the bound dissertation (one copy for each reviewer, one copy for the committee chair, and one copy for the FSC)
Digital version of the dissertation as a PDF
Certified copy of your university degree certificate and official diploma (unless already submitted with the declaration of intent to pursue a doctorate)
Signed, tabular CV
Statutory declaration
List of previous publications with an indication of your own contribution and one copy of each publication
In your application, you will propose your preferred reviewers. Please pay particular attention to Section 5(2) as well as Section 6(3) and (4) of the Doctoral Regulations: at least one of the reviewers must be a full-time professor in Faculty III; the second person must not be attached to the University (do not forget to provide their telephone number and email address). One of the reviewers cannot be a co-author. You may also submit a proposal for the person you would like to chair the doctoral committee. Please observe the requirements laid out in the Doctoral Regulations and discuss the proposal with your supervisor in advance.
Please send your documents by email before sending them by post or hand delivering them at an appointment with the Faculty Service Center.

Checklist for commencement of the doctoral procedure
Please note: if you use the title page template from the dissertation office of our library, please delete “genehmigte Dissertation”, because at this step of the procedure it isn't the final accepted thesis!
Review of the dissertation
As soon as you receive the letter confirming the commencement of your doctoral procedure, the reviewers have three months to individually and independently judge whether the submitted dissertation fulfills the requirements of a doctorate.
Once the dean has commenced the doctoral procedure, you can schedule the scientific defense with the reviewers and the chair of the doctoral committee. This may be scheduled before the Faculty Service Center receives the reviews and before the three-month deadline expires. Please inform the relevant staff member of the scheduled date as soon as possible (including the time and where it will take place) to determine the date by which the reviews must be submitted to the Faculty Service Center. If all expert reviews are available on that date, the faculty administration will send out the invitation to the scientific debate 16 days before it is scheduled to take place. Doctoral candidates will receive an invitation with various documents sent by registered mail to their address. The scientific defense must be postponed if the reviews are available less than 16 days before the scheduled date.
Scientific defense
Once the dean has commenced the doctoral procedure and the reviews have been received by the faculty administration, the scientific defense is held. This is the oral doctoral examination and is open to all University members. You will receive a preliminary certificate with the result of the doctorate afterwards.
Upcoming scientific defenses at the Faculty can be found here.
Publication of the dissertation and awarding of the doctorate
After the scientific defense, you are required to make the version approved by your TU supervisor (including any adjustments requested by the doctoral committee) available to the academic community within twelve months (extensions only in exceptional cases upon request).
The FAQ list of the University Library Dissertation Office with all important and frequently asked questions about the publication process of dissertations can be found here.
Find out more about the three possible forms of publication on the website of the Dissertation Office of the University Library of the TU Berlin:
1 printed copy + online publication on DepositOnce or
15 printed copies in classic dissertation printing or
3 publisher copies.
Select one of these options and follow the steps in the relevant checklist.
If you have any questions, please contact the Dissertation Office directly: dissertationen(at)ub.tu-berlin.de.
If it is a cumulative dissertation, further information, including copyright information, must be observed.
Once publication is complete, you will receive a confirmation of receipt from the Dissertation Office. This is usually sent directly to the faculty administration and is a prerequisite for receiving your doctoral certificate.
Submit the original signed confirmation from your supervisor regarding the changes you have made to the Faculty III Service Center so that the certificate (§10PromO) can be issued. You will receive this certificate together with two certified copies either in person or by mail, as agreed. Receipt of the certificate must be confirmed in writing.

Information and advising services
Junior research at the Faculty
The Faculty provides the latest news for junior scholars in WiMiNews, a newsletter which is sent by email on a near monthly basis. Please contact Research and Junior Scholars to sign up for the newsletter.
In order to motivate its junior scholars and recognize their work, Faculty III annually awards prizes for outstanding achievements: the doctoral award for junior researchers, two research awards (postdoc and doctoral candidates), and the teaching award. You can find information about the calls under “News” once applications have opened.
Continuing education and qualifications
Junior scholars at TU Berlin can avail of the offers of the University’s various organizational units and the BUA institutions for further training and qualifications. The courses can be found on the respective faculty websites.

Points of contact
The Center for Junior Scholars (CJS) is the first port of call for doctoral candidates and postdocs at Technische Universität Berlin.
You can find an overview of more useful contacts, from the Family Services Office to Psychological Counseling, here.
Contact
The Faculty Service Center is responsible for applications and answering questions about doctoral matters.
Ombudspersons for doctoral candidates are confidants for doctoral candidates. They can help you with problems and answer your questions.
Research and Junior Scholars is the point of contact for all matters relating to junior research and research funding at the Faculty.
From 1 April 2025, the elected representatives Julia Seilert and Jil Schwarze will represent the interests of internal and external doctoral candidates at the Faculty as the official doctoral candidate representatives. They can be reached via the functional address promovierende@fakultaet3-tu-berlin.de.
